title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: hoopR R package providing clean, tidy men’s basketball (NBA + Men’s College Basketball) play--play box score data. wraps NBA Stats API (stats.nba.com), ESPN API, KenPom, exporting ~576 functions. Primary source families: nba_*() (NBA Stats API), espn_nba_*() / espn_mbb_*() (ESPN), kp_*() (KenPom), cbbd_*() (CollegeBasketballData), bref_*() (Basketball Reference), torvik_*() (Bart Torvik), nbagl_*() (NBA G-League), ncaa_mbb_*() (NCAA), plus load_nba_*() / load_mbb_*() bulk loaders pull pre-built data sibling hoopR-data / sportsdataverse-data release repos. Sibling repos family: hoopR-data (NBA + MBB build/aggregate/publish), hoopR-mbb-raw / hoopR-mbb-data, hoopR-nba-raw / hoopR-nba-data, hoopR-nba-stats-raw / hoopR-nba-stats-data. guide differs current repository docs, treat CONTRIBUTING.md current test helper implementations authoritative. Version: 3.1.0 R Requirement: >= 4.1.0 License: MIT (CRAN + r-universe; pkgdown site https://hoopR.sportsdataverse.org) Branch: devel active development, main releases

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: Every NBA Stats API wrapper follows pattern: deprecated functions, add lifecycle documentation clear replacement path @description, enforce runtime lifecycle::deprecate_stop(). Prefer explicit imports keep minimal. Avoid package-wide @import directives unless required; remove unused imports refactoring files.
code: #' **Get NBA Stats API [Endpoint Name]** #' @name nba_functionname NULL #' @title #' **Get NBA Stats API [Endpoint Name]** #' @rdname nba_functionname #' @author Author Name #' @param game_id Game ID - 10-digit zero-padded ID (e.g., '0022200021') #' @param ... Additional arguments passed to the underlying function. #' @return Returns a named list of data frames: Component1, Component2 #' #'    **Component1** #' #' #'    |col_name |types     | #'    |:--------|:---------| #'    |column1  |character | #'    |column2  |integer   | #' #' @importFrom jsonlite fromJSON toJSON #' @importFrom dplyr filter select rename bind_cols bind_rows as_tibble #' @import rvest #' @export #' @family NBA Boxscore V3 Functions #' @details #' ```r #'  nba_functionname(game_id = "0022200021") #' ``` nba_functionname <- function(game_id = "0022200021", ...) {   endpoint <- nba_endpoint('endpointname')   full_url <- endpoint   params <- list(GameID = pad_id(game_id))    df_list <- list()  # Always initialize before tryCatch    tryCatch(     expr = {       resp <- request_with_proxy(url = full_url, params = params, ...)       # Parse response...       # Apply janitor::clean_names()       # Apply make_hoopR_data()       # Assign to df_list     },     error = function(e) {       message(glue::glue("{Sys.time()}: Invalid arguments or no data for {pad_id(game_id)} available!"))     },     warning = function(w) {},     finally = {}   )   return(df_list) }

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: V2: Returns resultSets[].headers[] + rowSet[][] (tabular). Parsed via nba_stats_map_result_sets(). V3: Returns nested JSON (e.g., game.actions[], boxScoreSummary.homeTeam.periods[]). Parsed via purrr::pluck() -> data.frame() -> pipeline. V3-style leader/standings endpoints: Return flat nested JSON arrays (e.g., dunks[], leaders[], teams[]). Parsed via purrr::pluck("key") -> dplyr::as_tibble() -> dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), .character)) -> janitor::clean_names() -> make_hoopR_data(). Examples: nba_dunkscoreleaders(), nba_gravityleaders(), nba_iststandings(). V3--V2 conversion pipeline (nba_pbp() V3 path): nba_playbyplayv3() -> .build_player_roster() -> .v3_to_v2_format() -> .players_on_court_v3(). produces V2-compatible columns (event_type, player1/2/3, etc.) retaining V3-columns (x_legacy, y_legacy, shot_distance, shot_result, is_field_goal, points_total, shot_value). V3 PBP single personId per action (player1_id/player2_id/player3_id like V2). V3 substitutions: actionType="Substitution", personId=outgoing player, description contains “SUB: IncomingPlayer OutgoingPlayer”. V3 clock format: ISO 8601 duration "PT10M30.00S" ("MM:SS"). Parsed base R regexec()/regmatches(). V3 -court players: .players_on_court_v3() uses nba_gamerotation() stint data interval mapping via findInterval() (substitution-event parsing like V2). NBAGL wrappers now use NBA Stats-backed sources several endpoints. nbagl_players() nbagl_standings() return named lists data frames (single data frames), nbagl_schedule() nbagl_pbp() expose current core columns active payloads.

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: Every wrapper returns variable assigned inside tryCatch must initialize variable tryCatch block. Otherwise, API errors (500s, timeouts, HTTP/2 stream errors, connection resets) error handler runs, return variable never bound, return(<var>) throws object '<var>' found instead intended cli::cli_alert_danger + empty fallback. rule applies every return variable name, just df_list: plays_df, pbp, standings, teams, team_box_score, athlete_roster_df, games, conferences, resp, data, etc. Initialize appropriate empty value — list() named-list returns, NULL single-object returns, data.frame() tibble returns.
code: nba_func <- function(...) {   endpoint <- nba_endpoint('foo')   params   <- list(...)    df_list <- list()   # <-- MANDATORY. Not inside tryCatch.    tryCatch(     expr = {       resp    <- request_with_proxy(url = endpoint, params = params, ...)       df_list <- nba_stats_map_result_sets(resp)     },     error = function(e) {       cli::cli_alert_danger("{Sys.time()}: Invalid arguments or no data available!")       cli::cli_alert_danger("Error:\n{e}")     },     warning = function(w) {       cli::cli_alert_warning("{Sys.time()}: Warning:\n{w}")     },     finally = {}   )   return(df_list) }

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: NBA Stats API ESPN’s JSON payloads add columns time without removing old ones, occasionally rename drop columns. Two guardrails apply: Inside functions — dropping known-transient column, use dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("colname")) instead dplyr::select(-"colname"). bare form errors moment upstream drops column; any_of -ops silently. Inside pipelines rename — use dplyr::rename(dplyr::any_of(c(new = "old"))) schema drift removes old survivable. See espn_mbb_conferences() ncaa_mbb_NET_rankings() examples.

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: HTTP requests use httr2 sole backend. httr package longer dependency. request_with_proxy() utils_nba_stats.R uses .retry_request() (httr2 wrapper) required NBA headers: - x-nba-stats-origin: stats - x-nba-stats-token: true - Referer: https://www.nba.com/ Shared internal helpers utils.R: - .retry_request(url, params, headers, timeout, proxy) – performs GET retry logic via httr2 - .resp_text(resp) – extracts response body UTF-8 text via httr2::resp_body_string() - check_status(res) – checks HTTP status via httr2::resp_status()

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: .retry_request() resolves proxy order: Explicit proxy = argument (caller-supplied; highest precedence). getOption("hoopR.proxy") session-level fallback — set options(hoopR.proxy = ...) every call picks . http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy environment variables — libcurl reads automatically explicit proxy supplied. proxy value (whether passed read option) accepts: - "http://host:port" — string form, forwarded httr2::req_proxy(url = ...). - list(url = "...", port = 8080, username = "...", password = "...", auth = "basic") — spread keyword args httr2::req_proxy() authenticated proxies. Per-call override works wrappers thread ... request_with_proxy() — ’s every NBA Stats API function (nba_*()), e.g. nba_pbp(game_id = "...", proxy = "http://-proxy:8080"). ESPN / KenPom / NBA G-League wrappers call .retry_request() directly without ..., use options() fallback env-var path. session option recommended pattern working one proxy across many calls — ’s single line top script covers everything. KenPom functions use separate httr2-based helpers: - login() – authenticates via httr2 cookie jar - .kp_get_page(jar, url) – fetches page parsed HTML - .kp_request(url, jar) – builds httr2 request KenPom headers nba_endpoint() builds URLs via glue::glue('https://stats.nba.com/stats/{endpoint}') – validate internal endpoint list.

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: Always use subset direction column assertions. upstream APIs add columns, strict expect_equal break new column. rule : expected list must subset actual columns. subset direction pattern survives upstream drift. Anti-patterns avoid: dynamic columns (like IST Standings game columns), expect_true((core_cols %% colnames(x))) equivalent subset-direction expect_in(). Per-element null checks: API sometimes returns fewer result sets test expects (e.g., 7 instead 11), use inline helper individual asserts skip gracefully rather erroring: See wehoop’s test-wnba_teamvsplayer.R test-wnba_playerdashboardbyclutch.R reference implementations helper pattern (direct hoopR analogue exists yet). NBAGL wrappers named-list returns, validate component names first validate core columns within component: deprecated wrappers, prefer explicit skip() replacement guidance test file avoid false negatives intentional hard stops. Use source-specific skip helper endpoint test: - skip_nba_stats_test() - skip_espn_test() - skip_nbagl_stats_test() - skip_ncaa_mbb_test() - skip_ncaa_wbb_test() - skip_kenpom_test()
code: test_that("NBA Endpoint Name", {   skip_on_cran()   skip_on_ci()   skip_nba_stats_test()  # Requires NBA_STATS_TESTS=1    x <- nba_function(game_id = "0022200021")    # Skip-if-empty guard — always right after the API call, before any assertions   # that touch x[[1]]. Handles transient 500s and HTTP/2 stream errors.   if (length(x) == 0 || is.null(x[[1]]) || !is.data.frame(x[[1]]) ||       nrow(x[[1]]) == 0) {     skip("No rows returned from endpoint at test time")   }    cols_x1 <- c("col1", "col2", ...)   expect_in(sort(cols_x1), sort(colnames(x[[1]])))   # expected ⊆ actual   expect_s3_class(x[[1]], "data.frame")    Sys.sleep(3)  # Rate limiting between tests }) # WRONG - flags when upstream adds a column, even though it's non-breaking expect_equal(sort(colnames(x[[1]])), sort(cols_x1))  # WRONG - same direction problem, just phrased with expect_in expect_in(sort(colnames(x[[1]])), sort(cols_x1)) check_cols <- function(i, cols) {   if (length(x) < i || is.null(x[[i]]) || !is.data.frame(x[[i]]) ||       ncol(x[[i]]) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))   expect_in(sort(cols), sort(colnames(x[[i]])))   expect_s3_class(x[[i]], "data.frame") } check_cols(1, cols_x1) check_cols(2, cols_x2) expect_true("Standings" %in% names(x)) expect_in(sort(core_cols), sort(colnames(x[[1]])))

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: hoopR 3.1.0 ships two families cross-source crosswalk builders backed shared internal engine R/crosswalk_basketball.R. Exported builders loaders (keyed espn_team_id): nba_team_crosswalk() / nba_schedule_crosswalk() / nba_player_crosswalk() — link ESPN, NBA Stats CDN (nba_schedule / nba_teams), Fox Sports identities. Note: NBA Stats CDN serves current season ; use load_nba_*_crosswalk() historical coverage. mbb_team_crosswalk() / mbb_schedule_crosswalk() / mbb_player_crosswalk() — link ESPN, KenPom (hoopR::teams_links bundled data — auth), Bart Torvik (barttorvik.com), Fox Sports identities. load_nba_*_crosswalk(seasons) / load_mbb_*_crosswalk(seasons) — cached loaders pull versioned .rds snapshots sportsdataverse-data release artifacts. fox_nba_teams() / fox_mbb_teams() / fox_mbb_teams_all() — Fox Bifrost team-directory enumerators. fox_mbb_teams_all() walks unseen conference seeds (max_calls standings calls) collect full MBB league. Internal .bb_* engine (R/crosswalk_basketball.R): .bb_normalize_team(x) — lowercase + strip punctuation; used NBA/Fox team-name keys. .bb_normalize_college_team(x) — extends .bb_normalize_team() contracting normalizer expands common abbreviations (“St.” → “State”, “St” → “Saint”, etc.) Torvik/KenPom terse names align ESPN. .bb_normalize_name(x) — player-name normalizer (lowercase, strip punctuation/suffixes) used within-block player matching. .bb_fuzzy_match(l, r, min_confidence) — deterministic Jaro-Winkler fuzzy match within team blocks: exact name first, JW jersey/DOB tiebreakers, unmatched. Returns left_id / right_id / match_method / match_confidence. .bb_to_eastern(x) — reduces UTC datetime local ET game date (used align ESPN Stats CDN dates schedule join key). MBB alias tables (R/mbb_crosswalk.R): .mbb_bart_alias — maps common Torvik terse team names ESPN location names (e.g. "Connecticut" → "UConn"). .mbb_kp_alias — shape, includes KenPom-specific divergences (e.g. "CSUN" → "Cal State Northridge"). .mbb_fox_display_alias — maps Fox normalized display names ESPN normalized display names strings diverge.

title: CLAUDE.md – hoopR Development Guide
text: pad_id() must called game IDs passing API (zero-pads 10 digits). V3 endpoints return different structures per endpoint – always verify nba_api Python parsers companion repo. data.frame(list_of_items) can produce unexpected column types API returns mixed NULL/value fields – use %||% defaults. @family tag groups functions pkgdown reference pages – keep consistent existing families. V3-style leader endpoints (dunkscoreleaders, gravityleaders) return values mixed types – coerce everything .character() %||% NA_character_ building data frames. IST Standings dynamic game columns (gameId1, gameId2, etc.) – tests use expect_true((core_cols %% colnames())) instead exact match. ESPN API columns change time – use expect_in() subset validation tests. NBA Stats V2 endpoints may return empty data certain games – tests handle empty results gracefully. Always initialize df_list <- list() (data <- data.frame() / data <- list()) tryCatch blocks avoid “object found” errors. .v3_to_v2_format() uses row-level loops player resolution – performance-sensitive large PBP datasets. %||% operator rlang used null-safe named vector lookups event type maps. .players_on_court_v3() depends nba_gamerotation() returning IN_TIME_REAL/OUT_TIME_REAL tenths second – ensure time unit consistency modifying. Local dev artifacts (example .vscode, .claude, ad-hoc logs) can surface R CMD check notes/warnings excluded build inputs. KenPom HTML structure changes periodically – CSS selectors tables (table#player-table), referee links (div.refline), navigation elements fragile may need updating. Two-block roxygen pattern + @noRd trap: internal helper uses @name + NULL topic block function-block, putting @noRd function block leaves topic block generate orphan man/dot-*.Rd file. pkgdown’s build_reference_index() fail “topics missing index”. Fix: put @keywords internal topic block well @noRd function block. Never hand-edit NAMESPACE files man/; regenerate devtools::document().

what: A note on the API surface
title: ESPN basketball endpoints -- NBA & MBB
text: ESPN exposes basketball data three public, unauthenticated API hosts, hoopR reaches : site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/{league} stable. serves scoreboards, teams, rosters, schedules, news, injuries, standings, player team season stats. sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/basketball/{league} carries deeper resources: athlete indexes, per-event detail (odds, win probabilities, officials, broadcasts), seasons, venues, coaches, NBA draft, transactions. Big collections paginate via $ref links. site.web.api.espn.com/apis/common/v3/sports/basketball/{league} carries per-athlete deep detail – season overview, stats category, game--game logs, situational splits. ’s least stable three; older seasons sometimes return 404, every athlete represented. ’s fourth host (cdn.espn.com/core) surfaces information site-v2 /summary endpoint already parse, don’t wrap . league slugs URL paths mens-college-basketball nba. matter ’re building requests hand. Rate limits. ESPN doesn’t publish . practice, requests arriving faster one per second occasionally come back HTTP 429 silently empty payloads. ’re looping many games athletes, drop Sys.sleep(1) calls. Proxies. ESPN wrappers don’t accept per-call proxy = argument; call package’s HTTP layer directly. Set proxy top session options(hoopR.proxy = "http://host:port") (list, authenticated proxies) every ESPN call pick automatically.

title: ESPN basketball endpoints -- NBA & MBB
text: endpoints exist ESPN deliberately wrapped: handful endpoints wrap known data quirks: espn_mbb_injuries() espn_mbb_team_injuries() – ESPN rarely populates injury data college basketball. espn_mbb_game_odds() – always empty; ESPN doesn’t carry NCAA lines. espn_nba_freeagents() – empty outside FA window. espn_*_athlete_awards() – sparse athletes. espn_*_athlete_eventlog() – returns $ref URLs, parsed stats. Use _athlete_gamelog() instead. espn_*_season_info() – mostly $ref URLs. web-common-v3 endpoints – legacy seasons return HTTP 404. something looks , empty tibble far often correct, expected return bug. ESPN’s basketball coverage uneven across leagues, seasons, franchise tenures, hoopR mirrors unevenness honestly rather papering .

text: ’re corporate campus network, traffic may need go proxy. hoopR understands proxies three layers, reach least invasive one works. Layer 1 – set whole session. want 99% time. covers every function package – ESPN, NBA Stats, KenPom, loaders, . Layer 2 – one call, one proxy. Every NBA Stats API function (nba_*) threads ... HTTP layer, can override proxy single call: grammar-flavored caveat: per-call proxy = works nba_* Stats API functions pass ... . espn_*, kp_*, load_* functions don’t take per-call proxy – , use session option Layer 1. prefix tells capability: nba_ functions ones wired per-call overrides. Layer 3 – let environment decide. ’d rather put proxy R code , hoopR honor standard environment variables: read libcurl automatically whenever haven’t set explicit proxy. ’s right layer shared scripts CI, proxy property machine, analysis.
code: # Plain proxy. options(hoopR.proxy = "http://proxy.company.com:8080")  # Authenticated proxy -- pass a list and it's spread into the request. options(hoopR.proxy = list(   url      = "http://proxy.company.com",   port     = 8080,   username = "saiem",   password = Sys.getenv("PROXY_PASS") ))  # From here on, nothing changes -- just call functions normally. espn_nba_team_roster(team_id = 13, season = most_recent_nba_season()) nba_leagueleaders(season = "2024-25") nba_leaguestandings(   season = "2024-25",   proxy  = "http://other-proxy.company.com:3128" ) #> list() Sys.setenv(   http_proxy  = "http://proxy.company.com:8080",   https_proxy = "http://proxy.company.com:8080",   no_proxy    = "localhost,127.0.0.1" )

title: hoopR Copilot Instructions
text: Follow tidyverse style: snake_case variables/functions, 2-space indentation. NBA Stats API functions use request_with_proxy() HTTP calls required NBA headers. Use %||% (rlang) null-safe defaults parsing API responses. returned data frames must pass janitor::clean_names() make_hoopR_data(). Use pad_id() game IDs passing API. Internal/non-exported helpers prefixed . (e.g., .players_on_court_v3()). Keep imports minimal explicit; remove unused imports (example, avoid @import furrr unless file actually uses ).

title: hoopR Copilot Instructions
text: HTTP requests use httr2 sole backend. httr package longer dependency. request_with_proxy() utils_nba_stats.R uses .retry_request() (httr2 wrapper) required NBA headers (x-nba-stats-origin, x-nba-stats-token, Referer). Shared internal helpers utils.R: .retry_request(), .resp_text(), check_status(). KenPom functions use httr2-based helpers: login() (cookie jar auth), .kp_get_page(), .kp_request(). nba_endpoint() builds URLs via paste0("https://stats.nba.com/stats/", endpoint) – validate internal endpoint list.

title: hoopR Copilot Instructions
text: .retry_request() resolves proxy order: explicit proxy = arg → getOption("hoopR.proxy") → libcurl env vars (http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy). Proxy value accepts URL string "http://host:port" named list list(url=, port=, username=, password=, auth=) spread httr2::req_proxy(). Per-call override (nba_foo(proxy = ...)) threads NBA Stats wrappers (forward ... request_with_proxy). ESPN / KenPom / NBA G-League wrappers call .retry_request() directly without ..., use options(hoopR.proxy = ...) session top — ’s recommended pattern session runs proxy.

title: hoopR Copilot Instructions
text: Use skip_on_cran(), skip_on_ci(), skip_nba_stats_test() guards. Use source-specific guards applicable: skip_espn_test(), skip_nbagl_stats_test(), skip_ncaa_mbb_test(), skip_ncaa_wbb_test(), skip_kenpom_test(). Column assertions must always use subset direction — expected ⊆ actual: expect_in(sort(expected_cols), sort(colnames(x))). NBA Stats ESPN APIs add columns without removing old ones, strict expect_equal(sort(colnames(x)), sort(cols)) flag new column. subset direction pattern survives upstream drift. Equivalently, expect_in(sort(colnames(x)), sort(expected)) also wrong — direction problem. dynamic columns, expect_true((core_cols %% colnames(x))) equivalent subset-direction expect_in(). Always add skip--empty guard immediately API call, assertion touches x[[1]]: handles transient 500s, HTTP/2 stream errors, empty responses without polluting failure report. tests assert multiple result sets (x[[1]]..x[[N]]) API sometimes returns fewer elements, wrap assertion per-index null/empty-column helper: See wehoop’s test-wnba_teamvsplayer.R reference implementation. deprecated wrappers, prefer explicit test skips replacement note rather brittle live assertions. Add Sys.sleep(3) end NBA Stats API tests rate limiting (~590 req/10 min). Test game ID: "0022200021" "0022201086" known completed games. Handle empty API responses gracefully tests (V2 endpoints may return empty old games).
code: x <- nba_func(...) if (length(x) == 0 || is.null(x[[1]]) || !is.data.frame(x[[1]]) ||     nrow(x[[1]]) == 0) {   skip("No rows returned from endpoint at test time") } check_cols <- function(i, cols) {   if (length(x) < i || is.null(x[[i]]) || !is.data.frame(x[[i]]) ||       ncol(x[[i]]) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))   expect_in(sort(cols), sort(colnames(x[[i]])))   expect_s3_class(x[[i]], "data.frame") }

Use --maxlevel 2 (level-3 sub-entries crowd nav). README.md. Rendered README.Rmd (output: github_document: { toc: true, toc_depth: 2 }). editing Rmd, run devtools::build_readme() commit README.Rmd + README.md together. Never hand-edit README.md. DESCRIPTION. editing DESCRIPTION (deps, versions, Authors@R, etc.), run usethis::use_tidy_description() normalize field order, alphabetize Imports/Suggests, reflow long lines. Run even one-line edits. Release notes triad — NEWS.md / cran-comments.md / _pkgdown.yml. Whenever add NEWS.md bullet, check two: NEWS.md — new bullets go recent unreleased version heading (currently # **hoopR 3.0.0**). create new version section ahead release; extend existing subsections (### Bug Fixes, ### Deprecations, ### Stability Test Robustness, …). release ships rule rolls forward next dev version. cran-comments.md — every user-visible / behavioral change NEWS.md reflected cran-comments.md submission. Internal-changes (refactors, test infra, dev tooling) can omitted. _pkgdown.yml — new exports go right reference: section. starts_with() selectors auto-pick nba_* / espn_* / kp_* / ncaa_* prefixes; explicitly-listed functions need manual entry. lifecycle::deprecate_stop() + @keywords internal excludes function rendered index default.

title: hoopR Copilot Instructions
text: V3 endpoints return nested JSON – use purrr::pluck() extraction. V3 PBP clock format "PT10M30.00S" "MM:SS". Parsed base R regexec()/regmatches(). V3 PBP substitutions: personId = outgoing player, incoming parsed “SUB: IncomingPlayer OutgoingPlayer” description. V3--V2 conversion pipeline (nba_pbp() V3 path): nba_playbyplayv3() -> .build_player_roster() -> .v3_to_v2_format() -> .players_on_court_v3(). Produces V2-compatible columns retaining V3-columns (x_legacy, y_legacy, shot_distance, shot_result, is_field_goal, points_total, shot_value). .players_on_court_v3() uses nba_gamerotation() stint data interval mapping (substitution-event parsing like V2). V3 boxscore endpoints namespace: boxscoretraditionalv3, boxscoreadvancedv3, etc. V3-style leader/standings endpoints (dunkscoreleaders, gravityleaders, iststandings) return flat nested JSON arrays. Parse via purrr::pluck("key") -> dplyr::as_tibble() -> dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), .character)) -> janitor::clean_names(). V3-style schedule endpoint (scheduleleaguev2int) follows nested structure nba_schedule(). NBAGL wrappers can follow NBA Stats-backed payloads. particular, nbagl_players() nbagl_standings() may return named lists data frames (e.g., PlayerIndex, Standings) rather single flat data frame.

title: hoopR Copilot Instructions
text: hoopR 3.1.0 adds cross-source crosswalk builders backed shared engine R/crosswalk_basketball.R. crosswalks keyed espn_team_id. NBA: nba_team_crosswalk() / nba_schedule_crosswalk() / nba_player_crosswalk() link ESPN, NBA Stats CDN, Fox. NBA Stats CDN serves current season ; use load_nba_*_crosswalk() history. MBB: mbb_team_crosswalk() / mbb_schedule_crosswalk() / mbb_player_crosswalk() link ESPN, KenPom (hoopR::teams_links, auth), Bart Torvik, Fox. fox_mbb_teams_all() enumerates full MBB Fox Bifrost directory via conference-seed walking. Cached loaders: load_nba_*_crosswalk(seasons) / load_mbb_*_crosswalk(seasons) pull versioned .rds snapshots sportsdataverse-data release artifacts. .bb_* engine conventions: Matching deterministic: exact normalized name within team block, Jaro-Winkler fuzzy (min_confidence = 0.92) jersey/DOB tiebreakers. .bb_normalize_college_team() contracting normalizer expands “St.” → “State” / “St” → “Saint” Torvik/KenPom terse names align ESPN. Dates reduced local ET game date via .bb_to_eastern() joining schedule crosswalk key. MBB alias tables (.mbb_bart_alias, .mbb_kp_alias, .mbb_fox_display_alias mbb_crosswalk.R) bridge source-specific name divergences normalization. adding new source, add curated alias table builder file wrap fetch tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL) empty-typed fallback frame ESPN always anchors even partial failures.

title: hoopR Copilot Instructions
text: Return-value initialization mandatory: every wrapper return(X) X assigned inside tryCatch(expr = {...}) must initialize X tryCatch. Otherwise, API errors, return(X) throws object 'X' found instead intended empty fallback. Applies df_list, plays_df, pbp, standings, teams, team_box_score, athlete_roster_df, games, conferences, resp, data, etc. — return variable. Initialize list() named-list returns, NULL single-object returns, data.frame() tibble returns. dropping known-transient column inside function, use dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("colname")) instead dplyr::select(-"colname"). bare form errors moment upstream drops column. renaming columns janitor::clean_names(), use dplyr::rename(dplyr::any_of(c(new = "old"))) function survives upstream rename/drops without breaking. See espn_mbb_conferences() ncaa_mbb_NET_rankings() examples. ESPN API columns change time — column assertions tests must use subset direction (expect_in(expected, actual)). V3-style leader endpoints return mixed types – coerce .character() %||% NA_character_. IST Standings dynamic game columns – use expect_true((core_cols %% colnames())). NBAGL legacy schemas longer stable references tests. Prefer validating core columns current API payloads handle named-list returns explicitly tests. Local editor/worktree artifacts (e.g., .vscode, .claude, temp logs) can cause R CMD check notes/warnings included source checks. KenPom HTML structure changes periodically – CSS selectors tables (table#player-table), referee links (div.refline), navigation elements fragile may need updating. Two-block roxygen pattern + @noRd trap: internal helper uses @name + NULL topic block function-block, putting @noRd function block leaves topic block generate orphan man/dot-*.Rd file. pkgdown’s build_reference_index() fail “topics missing index”. Fix: put @keywords internal topic block well @noRd function block. Never edit NAMESPACE man/ files hand; regenerate devtools::document().

what: hoopR: Access Men's Basketball Play by Play Data — hoopR-package
title: hoopR: Access Men's Basketball Play by Play Data — hoopR-package
text: utility quickly obtain clean tidy men's basketball play play data. Provides functions access live play play box score data ESPNhttps://www.espn.com shot locations available. also full NBA Stats APIhttps://www.nba.com/stats/ wrapper. also scraping aggregating interface Ken Pomeroy's men's college basketball statistics websitehttps://kenpom.com. provides users active subscription capability scrape website tables analyze data .

title: HoopsHype Player Salaries — hoopshype_salaries
text: Get NBA player salaries HoopsHype. Returns full league's player salaries, one row per player per contract season (current plus future seasons HoopsHype lists). API key required; dollar figures returned numeric. HoopsHype Next.js app whose single salaries page paginates client-side, team's salary page (/salaries/{team}/) embeds team's complete roster __NEXT_DATA__ payload. function iterates 30 team pages stitches together (≈30 requests per call) using team--team approach.

code: nba_bind_sets(result_sets, tag_column = "set_name")  nba_join_sets(result_sets, join_key)  nba_nest_sets(result_sets, keep_cols, nest_col = ".data")

title: Reduce NBA Stats API result sets — nba_bind_sets
text: result_sets named list tibbles (nba_*() return). tag_column Name origin column nba_bind_sets() adds (holds set names). Defaults "set_name". join_key Single shared column name nba_join_sets() joins sets . keep_cols Grouping key column(s) nba_nest_sets() keeps wide; every column nested. nest_col Name list-column nba_nest_sets() creates. Defaults ".data".

title: Reduce NBA Stats API result sets — nba_bind_sets
text: single tbl_df (bound, joined, nested).

title: Reduce NBA Stats API result sets — nba_bind_sets
text: nba_bind_sets() row-binds sets one long tibble, tagging row origin (tactic B). Use sets share schema, simply want stacked origin column (e.g. draft rounds, per-mode stat blocks). Columns absent given set fill NA. nba_join_sets() successively left-joins sets one wide tibble shared key (tactic C). Use sets different facets entity (e.g. player stats + team stats keyed game player id). nba_nest_sets() keeps keep_cols (plus set name) wide nests every column list-column, preserving data single flat schema can hold (tactic D). Use incompatible sets (e.g. player profile's season totals + career totals + awards). Recover set tidyr::unnest(). three accept named list tibbles – nba_*() return, output nba_stats_map_result_sets() – return single tibble.

title: Reduce NBA Stats API result sets — nba_bind_sets
code: sets <- list(   PlayerStats = data.frame(GAME_ID = "1", PERSON_ID = c(1, 2), PTS = c(10, 20)),   TeamStats   = data.frame(GAME_ID = "1", TEAM_ID = 99, PTS = 30) ) nba_bind_sets(sets, tag_column = "set")          # B: row-bind + tag #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   set         GAME_ID PERSON_ID   PTS TEAM_ID #>   <chr>       <chr>       <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 PlayerStats 1               1    10      NA #> 2 PlayerStats 1               2    20      NA #> 3 TeamStats   1              NA    30      99 nba_join_sets(sets, join_key = "GAME_ID")        # C: join/widen on a key #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   GAME_ID PERSON_ID PTS.x TEAM_ID PTS.y #>   <chr>       <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 1               1    10      99    30 #> 2 1               2    20      99    30 nba_nest_sets(sets, keep_cols = "GAME_ID")       # D: nest into a list-column #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   set_name    GAME_ID .data            #>   <chr>       <chr>   <list>           #> 1 PlayerStats 1       <tibble [2 × 3]> #> 2 TeamStats   1       <tibble [1 × 3]>

text: Fetches leaguedashptstats dashboards combination seasons season_types, aggregates results entity (PLAYER_ID Player, TEAM_ID Team) following contract ported sportsdataverse-py's aggregate_tracking_frames: Identity columns (*_ID, *_NAME, *_ABBREVIATION, non-numeric string column TEAM_CITY) carried via first() — never summed. *_FG_PCT / *_FT_PCT recomputed summed FGM/FGA FTM/FTA denominators (denom 0 → NA); *_FG_PCT / *_FT_PCT column whose makes/attempts pair absent dropped rather recomputed. *_PCT columns (e.g., DRIVE_PTS_PCT — "% total" rates) dropped output additive. remaining numeric columns summed (numeric-content gate, mirroring sportsdataverse-py dtype.is_numeric() rule).

title: Aggregate NBA Player-Tracking Stats Across Multiple Seasons — nba_tracking_aggregate
text: seasons Character vector NBA season strings, e.g. c("2022-23", "2023-24"). season_types Character vector season type(s), e.g. "Regular Season" c("Regular Season", "Playoffs"). Defaults "Regular Season". per_mode Per-mode string passed nba_leaguedashptstats (default "Totals"). Use "Totals" aggregation; per-game averages meaningfully additive. pt_measure_type Tracking measure type string, e.g. "Drives", "SpeedDistance", "Passing". Passed directly nba_leaguedashptstats. Default "Drives". player_or_team "Player" (default) "Team". Determines entity key used group aggregation (PLAYER_ID TEAM_ID). league_id League identifier string. Default "00" (NBA). ... Additional arguments forwarded nba_leaguedashptstats (e.g., date_from, date_to, conference).

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: Development release top CRAN-shipped 3.0.0 (commit b76100b3). Headline change 58-wrapper ESPN endpoint expansion brings hoopR’s ESPN coverage parity wehoop — athlete coverage, team detail, event detail, league catalog, news, calendar, injuries, plus draft / freeagents / transactions NBA. Also includes bug fixes endpoint behavior drifted CRAN submission, package-wide @return documentation upgrade, proxy-support restoration addresses regression introduced 3.0.0 httr → httr2 migration.

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: New convenience functions link team / schedule / player identities across ESPN, NBA Stats API, Fox Sports shared espn_team_id key: nba_team_crosswalk(), nba_schedule_crosswalk() (joins local Eastern-Time game date), nba_player_crosswalk() (ESPN-anchored deterministic fuzzy matching), paired load_nba_*_crosswalk() cached loader. Adds fox_nba_teams() / fox_mbb_teams() deriving Fox team directory standings endpoint. shared internal .bb_* matching engine (R/crosswalk_basketball.R) backs builders.

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: New convenience functions link team / schedule / player identities across ESPN, KenPom (teams_links bundled data — auth required), Bart Torvik (barttorvik.com), Fox Sports shared espn_team_id key: mbb_team_crosswalk(), mbb_schedule_crosswalk() (joins ET game date via Torvik’s game schedule), mbb_player_crosswalk() (ESPN-anchored deterministic fuzzy matching vs. Fox), paired load_mbb_*_crosswalk() cached loader. Torvik KenPom team names bridged ESPN via curated alias tables (.mbb_bart_alias, .mbb_kp_alias) .bb_normalize_college_team() contracting normalizer (expands State/Saint abbreviations). Fox names bridged via .mbb_fox_display_alias. Adds fox_mbb_teams_all() enumerate full MBB Fox Bifrost team directory (conference-seed walking). Backed shared .bb_* engine R/crosswalk_basketball.R.

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: Read-Fox Sports “Bifrost” basketball wrappers api.foxsports.com/bifrost/v1/{nba,cbk}/*, complementing espn_nba_* / espn_mbb_* families. Eight wrappers per league flatten Fox’s layout-oriented JSON (sections → tables → rows → cells) tidy hoopR_data tibbles: fox_<lg>_pbp (period-based play--play), _boxscore, _odds, _team_roster, _team_stats, _team_gamelog, _standings, _league_leaders. shared internal layer backs leagues. Verified live; reverse-engineering notes + OpenAPI 3.1 spec live sdv-internal-refs repo. Parallels cfbfastR / sportsdataverse-py fox_* families.

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: New cbbd_*() function family wrapping CollegeBasketballData API (men’s college basketball sibling CollegeFootballData, cfbfastR wraps cfbd_*). 38 endpoint wrappers cover full v1 surface across 13 categories: Games: cbbd_games(), cbbd_games_media(), cbbd_games_teams(), cbbd_games_players(), cbbd_scoreboard() Plays: cbbd_plays_game(), cbbd_plays_player(), cbbd_plays_team(), cbbd_plays_date(), cbbd_plays_tournament(), cbbd_play_types() Substitutions: cbbd_substitutions_game(), cbbd_substitutions_player(), cbbd_substitutions_team() Stats: cbbd_stats_team_season(), cbbd_stats_team_leaderboard(), cbbd_stats_team_shooting_season(), cbbd_stats_player_season(), cbbd_stats_player_shooting_season() Lineups: cbbd_lineups_team(), cbbd_lineups_game() Ratings: cbbd_ratings_srs(), cbbd_ratings_adjusted(), cbbd_ratings_elo() Rankings: cbbd_rankings() Lines: cbbd_lines(), cbbd_lines_providers() Recruiting: cbbd_recruiting_players(), cbbd_recruiting_teams(), cbbd_recruiting_portal() Draft: cbbd_draft_teams(), cbbd_draft_positions(), cbbd_draft_picks() Teams / Venues / Conferences: cbbd_teams(), cbbd_teams_roster(), cbbd_venues(), cbbd_conferences(), cbbd_conferences_history() API requires free Bearer-token key stored CBBD_API_KEY environment variable; see ?register_cbbd. Helpers cbbd_key(), has_cbbd_key() check_cbbd_key() mirror cfbfastR key pattern. Every wrapper returns hoopR_data tibble 3-column @return table, routes hoopR’s shared httr2 request layer (retries / timeouts / proxy), reports errors via standard cli reporters.

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: New torvik_*() function family pulling publicly available men’s college basketball data directly barttorvik.com — account API key required (analogous kp_* scrapes KenPom). wrap auth-free, self-describing data files (interactive .php pages behind barttorvik’s JavaScript browser check intentionally avoided): torvik_ratings() — year-end / current T-Rank team ratings: adjusted offensive/defensive efficiency, barthag, projected record, SOS, wins bubble, adjusted tempo ({year}_team_results.csv). torvik_team_factors() — team four factors shooting splits: eFG%, TOV%, OREB%/DREB%, FT rate, 2P/3P/FT splits assist rates, national rank ({year}_fffinal.csv). torvik_game_schedule() — full game--game schedule results pre-game predictions post-game quality metrics ({year}_super_sked.json). torvik_ncaa_results() — historical NCAA tournament performance team, coach, conference seed, including PASE / PAKE round--round counts (cgi-bin/ncaat.cgi). torvik_player_stats() — every player’s advanced season stat line: offensive rating, usage, shooting splits, rebounding/assist/turnover rates, box plus/minus per-game box averages (getadvstats.php). torvik_game_stats() — per-team-game stats: adjusted raw offensive/defensive efficiency, four factors ends, tempo, result pre-game win probability (getgamestats.php). Requests route hoopR’s shared .retry_request() layer browser User-Agent; every wrapper returns hoopR_data tibble 3-column @return table reports errors via standard cli reporters. (Note: cbbdata/api.cbbdata.com service previously brokered Torvik data defunct, wrap barttorvik.com directly.)

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: New bref_*() function family scraping publicly available NBA data Basketball-Reference — source hoopR previously cover (account API key required): bref_players_stats() — league-wide player season stats; pick table table = "per_game" / "totals" / "advanced" / "per_minute" / "per_poss". bref_teams_stats() — team season stats (per_game, totals, per_poss, advanced, opponent). bref_standings() — end--season conference standings SRS playoff flag. bref_draft() — draft results paired pick’s career totals advanced metrics. bref_awards() — end--season award voting (MVP, ROY, DPOY, SMOY, MIP, Clutch POY, COY) one tidy tibble. bref_team_roster() — team’s season roster. bref_player_game_log() — player’s game--game log season (Basketball-Reference player-id slug, e.g. jokicni01). bref_player_bios() — player index starting letter (career span, position, height/weight, birth date, college) plus player’s Basketball-Reference id slug — ready-made player dictionary. bref_injuries() — current Basketball-Reference NBA injury report. Two Sports-Reference quirks handled centrally: secondary tables hidden HTML comments un-commented, columns read cell’s data-stat attribute (multi-row “-headers” don’t mangle column names). Routes hoopR’s shared .retry_request() browser User-Agent. Basketball-Reference rate-limits aggressive scraping (~20 requests/minute) — space repeated calls Sys.sleep(). Tests gated behind BREF_TESTS=1. new dependencies (rvest already Imports).

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: New wrappers third-party NBA salary mock-draft sites, public HTML, key required: spotrac_team_cap() — team salary-cap allocations, cap space, active players average age Spotrac. hoopshype_salaries() — full league’s player salaries (one row per player-season, current + future contract years) HoopsHype. HoopsHype now Next.js app whose single salaries page paginates client-side, team page embeds team’s complete roster __NEXT_DATA__ payload — iterates 30 team pages stitches together (~600 players) via team--team approach. nbadraft_mock_draft() — current consensus mock draft (rounds) NBADraft.net. Basketball Insiders evaluated wrapped: old salary-widget backend (hw-files.com) offline, surviving page exposes team-cap summary redundant spotrac_team_cap(). league-wide player salaries, espn_nba_player_contracts() remains complete source.

what: RealGM (realgm_*) — Cloudflare-challenge bypass via headless Chrome
title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: RealGM sits behind Cloudflare JavaScript challenge (cf-mitigated: challenge) returns HTTP 403 every libcurl-based client (httr2, httr, rvest) regardless headers — Cloudflare fingerprints TLS handshake (JA3) demands JavaScript proof--work mint cf_clearance cookie. earlier source audit recorded RealGM dead basis. dead — reachable real browser engine, 17 realgm_*() wrappers now cover NBA endpoint surface: Players & personnel realgm_players() — active NBA player index (position, ht/wt, age, current team, years service, pre-draft team / international club, nationality). realgm_players_abroad() — NBA-affiliated players international rosters, NBA-rights status (view first-party feed provides). realgm_future_free_agents() — projected free-agent classes Bird / veteran status, production, player’s listed agent. realgm_coaches() / realgm_gms() — current head coaches / general managers tenure nationality. Standings, teams & stats realgm_standings() — conferences record, streak, splits. realgm_teams() — team index division conference. realgm_player_stats(season, stat_type, season_type) — qualified-player leaderboards (Averages / Totals / Per-X / Advanced / Misc, across Regular Season / Playoffs / Preseason / Summer League). realgm_team_stats(season, stat_type, season_type) — team statistics. realgm_individual_seasons() / realgm_individual_games() — -time best individual season / single-game leaderboards. Draft & salary realgm_draft(year) — past-draft results (rounds 1–2 + undrafted), pre-draft team nationality. realgm_draft_prospects() — current draft-prospect statistics. realgm_early_entry() — early-entrant / withdrawal list. realgm_salary_cap() — salary-cap history & projections (cap, tax, aprons, exceptions). realgm_rookie_scale() — rookie-scale contract amounts pick. Transactions realgm_transactions() — league transactions log (RealGM publishes dated narrative, table, parses page DOM one row per transaction real Date). Self-describing returns carry query parameters back columns (realgm_player_stats()/realgm_team_stats() echo season/stat_type/ season_type; realgm_draft() echoes draft_year round label). Every wrapper drives headless Chrome optional chromote package (Chrome solves challenge natively ~2 seconds). chromote + Google Chrome therefore Suggests-level requirement realgm_* family ; every hoopR source still works standard HTTP stack.

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: hoopR’s NBA Stats wrappers return endpoint’s resultSets verbatim named list tibbles (structure-faithful, lossless). three pure helpers reduce list single tibble demand — making explicit, composable, three common result-set reductions: nba_bind_sets(tag_column = ) — row-bind sets one long tibble, tagging row origin (tactic B); columns absent set fill NA. sets share schema, stack tag. nba_join_sets(join_key = ) — successively left-join sets one wide tibble shared key (tactic C). different facets one entity (e.g. PlayerStats + TeamStats GAME_ID). nba_nest_sets(keep_cols = , nest_col = ) — keep key column(s) wide nest every column list-column, preserving set origin (tactic D). heterogeneous sets can’t bound joined (e.g. player profile’s season totals / career totals / awards). three take named list tibbles (nba_*() return) always return tibble. default hoopR return (list ) “keep ” option.

title: hoopR 3.1.0
text: package migrated httr httr2 3.0.0, legacy httr::use_proxy() plumbing dropped request_with_proxy() quietly stopped honoring proxies (... preserved purely source compatibility). request_with_proxy() lower-level .retry_request() now accept proxy = argument: proxy = NULL (default) — libcurl reads http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy env vars automatically. proxy = "http://host:port" — string form, forwarded httr2::req_proxy(url = ...). proxy = list(url=, port=, username=, password=, auth=) — named list spread httr2::req_proxy() authenticated proxies. Resolution order .retry_request(): explicit proxy = arg → getOption("hoopR.proxy") → libcurl env vars. ... thread works NBA Stats wrappers (forward request_with_proxy()); ESPN / KenPom / NBA G-League wrappers call .retry_request() directly without ..., use options(hoopR.proxy = ...) top session cover without per-function plumbing.
